requirements.requirement: Configure opsadmin on node1 for SSH access with the supplied ED25519 public key.
requirements.summary: The opsadmin account exists with the expected home and shell; the supplied key is installed with secure ownership, permissions, and SELinux labeling. Its fingerprint and comment remained intact after reboot.

Effective sshd policy requires publickey authentication and disables password and keyboard-interactive authentication. Live probes before and after reboot reached the server and advertised only publickey; sshd remained active and listening.

overall_summary: Both material outcomes are satisfied. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete for node1: it captures the healthy pre-restart state and boot ID, restart acknowledgement, a different post-restart boot ID, and recovered system, sshd, account, key, policy, and listener state. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the reboot.
limitations: No successful login using the matching private key was captured; the live probes intentionally supplied no credential and therefore validate that only publickey authentication is offered, while login readiness is supported by the directly observed account, authorized key, permissions, SELinux label, and effective sshd configuration.

operational_hygiene.summary: All observed mutations had clear task or evidence roles: account/key creation and password locking (cmd-d8b49c70ad774630), sshd policy installation and reload (cmd-a36f7fae05a34b51), and the mandatory evidence reboot (cmd-05c79957156940dd). No unnecessary mutation was identified. Final snapshots show no failed services, healthy package state, unchanged service exposure apart from expected post-reboot process identifiers, and only normal reboot-generated temporary directories.
